lessons.title: What Does Nocturnal Mean?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain that nocturnal animals are awake at night and asleep in the day.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children do at night vs day.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce nocturnal animals (owl, bat, hedgehog, fox) with pictures, sorting into 'day' and 'night' animal groups.
key_questions: Which animals are awake at night?
Why might an animal prefer to be awake at night?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of nocturnal concept — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look for a nocturnal animal (or signs of one) near your home.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Owl Babies' by Martin Waddell
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how the owl babies felt while their mother was away.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'Owl Babies', discussing the characters' feelings of worry and relief.
key_questions: How did the owl babies feel?
How did they feel when mother returned?

differentiation.support: Point to feeling faces to answer

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional comprehension — evidence for LIT.1/PSED.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you felt worried and then relieved.

lessons.title: Counting the Owl Babies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count a small group of three and beyond accurately.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the three owl babies (Sarah, Percy, Bill).
lessons.main_activity: Children count sets of owl counters/pictures up to 5-10, checking accuracy.
key_questions: How many owls are there?
Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Count objects in groups of 3 at home.

lessons.title: Owl Feather Collage
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to arrange and stick materials to create an owl's feathered texture.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at real/picture owl feathers.
lessons.main_activity: Children create an owl picture using layered paper 'feathers' or torn tissue paper for texture.
resources_needed: Owl body template, coloured paper/tissue paper, glue
key_questions: How did you create the feather texture?
What colours did you use?

differentiation.extension: Tear/cut own feather shapes and layer carefully

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor and texture representation — evidence for EAD.1/PD.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at bird feathers on a walk together.

lessons.title: How Do Owls See and Hear in the Dark?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one special feature that helps owls hunt at night.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at close-up pictures of an owl's eyes.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss owl adaptations (big eyes for night vision, silent flight, good hearing) using pictures/simple facts.
key_questions: Why does an owl have big eyes?
How does an owl fly so quietly?

differentiation.support: Share one adaptation fact with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of animal adaptation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look up a fact about owls together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'v'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'v' and blend words (van, vet, vat).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'v' sound/action; blend new CVC words.
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend v-a-n?
lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'v'.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending van, vet, vat.

lessons.title: Sorting Nocturnal vs Day Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort animals into two groups using one criterion.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap nocturnal vs day animals from Monday.
lessons.main_activity: Children sort a mixed set of animal picture cards into nocturnal and daytime groups, counting each group.
key_questions: How many nocturnal animals did you find?
How did you decide where to sort each one?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sorting and counting skill — evidence for MATHS.2/MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Sort toy animals into day/night groups at home.

lessons.title: Moving Like Nocturnal Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move imaginatively like different nocturnal animals.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how an owl flies silently vs a bat flutters.
lessons.main_activity: Children move around the space imitating owls swooping, bats fluttering, and foxes creeping silently.
key_questions: How does an owl move?
Can you move silently like a fox?

differentiation.extension: Invent an original nocturnal animal movement

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.home_link: Act out a nocturnal animal for family.

lessons.title: Exploring Owl Pellets (Simulated)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make an observation about what owls eat.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what owls might eat (mice, small animals).
lessons.main_activity: (Using simulated/model pellets or picture diagrams) children explore what an owl pellet contains and discuss owl diet.
key_questions: What do you think an owl eats?
What did you find in the pellet?

differentiation.extension: Describe the food chain simply (owl eats mouse)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note investigative and scientific observation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look up what your favourite animal eats together.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Owl Who Was Afraid of the Dark'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how the character overcame their fear.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss things that can feel scary in the dark.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, discussing how Plop the owl learns the dark isn't so scary.
key_questions: Why was Plop afraid?
How did Plop's feelings change?

differentiation.extension: Explain reasoning for the character's changing feelings

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional comprehension and reasoning — evidence for LIT.1/PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss things that help us feel less scared of the dark.
lessons.home_link: Talk about ways to feel less scared of the dark at home.

lessons.title: Owl Eyes: Counting in Twos
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in twos using owl eyes as a visual model.
lessons.starter_activity: Count eyes of children in the class (in pairs).
lessons.main_activity: Children count owl pictures with two eyes each, practising counting in twos (2, 4, 6, 8...) up to 10.
resources_needed: Owl picture cards with visible eyes
key_questions: How many eyes does one owl have? Two owls?
Can you count in twos?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early skip-counting understanding — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap counting in twos together.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting pairs of things (shoes, socks) at home.

lessons.title: Owl Eyes Printing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use circular printing objects to create owl eyes on their collage.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at round objects available for printing (lids, cups).
lessons.main_activity: Children print circular 'eyes' onto their owl collage from Monday using round objects dipped in paint.
resources_needed: Round lids/cups, paint, Monday's owl collage
key_questions: What did you use to print the eyes?
Are the eyes the same size?

differentiation.extension: Add pupils/detail to the printed eyes

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe printing technique and shape awareness — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display completed owl collages with eyes added.
lessons.home_link: Look for circular objects around your home to print with.

lessons.title: Where Do Owls Live? Habitats
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe where owls make their homes.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap 'Owl Babies' — where did the owls live?
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and look at pictures of different owl habitats (tree holes, barns, nest boxes).
key_questions: Where do owls make their home?
Why might an owl choose a tree hole?

differentiation.extension: Compare 3+ habitat types and reason why

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of habitats — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look for bird nests or nest boxes on a walk together.

lessons.title: Writing Owl Sound Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write the sound an owl makes ('twit twoo').
lessons.starter_activity: Practise making owl sounds together.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw an owl and attempt to write 'hoot' or similar sound words using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What sound does an owl make?
Can you write that word?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share owl sound pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Practise owl hooting sounds together and write the word.

lessons.title: Number Bonds to 5 Recap: Nocturnal Animal Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 5 fluently.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire number bonds to 5 quiz.
lessons.main_activity: Using owl/bat counters, children practise and record all number bonds to 5 in a nocturnal-animal context.
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 5?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond fluency progress — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 5.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 5 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Nocturnal Animals Shadow Play
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create and describe shadow shapes representing nocturnal animals.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the torch/shadow exploration from Week 10.
lessons.main_activity: Using a torch and screen/wall, children create hand shadow shapes representing nocturnal animals (owl, bat) and perform a simple shadow story.
key_questions: What shadow shape can you make?
Can you make it move like the animal?

differentiation.support: Adult models a simple shadow shape

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative shadow play — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform shadow shapes for each other.
lessons.home_link: Make hand shadows with a torch at home in the evening.

lessons.title: Nocturnal Animals Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about nocturnal animals learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's UTW learning.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Nocturnal Animals' display summarising owl facts, adaptations, and habitats.
key_questions: What did we learn about nocturnal animals?
What was most interesting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about nocturnal animals with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: All 20 Sounds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read CVC words and simple sentences using all sounds learned so far.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard review of all 20 sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building, CVC reading cards, simple sentence reading (e.g. 'the owl can hoot').
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 12 phonics tracker.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all sounds learned with a reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading simple sentences over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Sorting, Number Bonds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, sorting, and number bond skills learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting owls, sorting nocturnal/day animals, number bonds to 5.
key_questions: How many is this?
Which group does this belong to?
What makes 5?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 12 maths observations.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising sorting and counting over the weekend.

lessons.title: Nocturnal Animals Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine movement, shadow play, and craft in a short class performance.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining nocturnal animal movements, owl sounds, and shadow shapes, with owl collages displayed.
resources_needed: Craft from the week, torch for shadows
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the nocturnal animals week.
lessons.home_link: Perform a nocturnal animal movement for family this weekend.
